annotations.annotation_text: The Letter motif "letter" on page 211 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): ALP's mysterious document — scratched from the midden by Biddy Doran the Hen — represents the genesis of all writing within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. During this Age of Gods (closing) phase, the letter functions simultaneously as archaeological artifact, love note, legal deposition, and the text of Finnegans Wake itself.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Deane, Vincent, et al. The Finnegans Wake Notebooks at Buffalo. https://www.brepols.net

annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Shaun" on page 211 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Gods (closing) phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
